source.title: Logit Attenuating Weight Normalization
source.authors: Aman Gupta; R. Ramanath; Jun Shi; Anika Ramachandran; Sirou Zhou; Mingzhou Zhou; S. Keerthi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; some PDF extraction artifacts (for example, a missing figure number) do not affect the extracted results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizer and batch-size conditions using held-out performance, but does not measure the training-to-test gap itself or use the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy and recommendation HR@10, not training error or a train–test gap. It does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. LAWN comparisons in Tables 1–4 and the CIFAR/recommendation tables are extracted where they bear on optimizer or batch-size versions; other loss-adaptivity comparisons are noted under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out image-classification results comparing adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD and comparing batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets. These test V4 and V5 without requiring a measured train–test gap. Its LAWN-versus-base comparisons alone do not establish either optimizer rankings against SGD or a batch-size effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that switching from free to fixed weight-norm training improves adaptivity and held-out performance across image-classification and recommendation tasks, highlighting Adam and large-batch training. This is their overall conclusion; individual tables include negligible improvements, residual batch penalties, and recommendation failures for SGD variants.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces LAWN, which switches from unconstrained to projected, fixed weight-norm training; evaluates optimizers and batch sizes rather than testing the original claims directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with optimizer, batch size, dataset, LAWN switch point, learning-rate schedule, and tuning choices. For ImageNet the epoch budget is fixed at 90; recommendation experiments use 300 epochs for the two smallest batch sizes and 500 for the two largest.

fits_no_version.finding: Same-batch LAWN-versus-base comparisons report improvements in held-out image accuracy, especially for Adam; these comparisons alone do not measure the optimizer ranking against SGD or the effect of batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Switching to constrained weight-norm training can improve held-out image accuracy relative to the corresponding base optimizer.

fits_no_version.finding: On recommendation tasks, Adam-LAWN and LAMB-LAWN generally retain HR@10 across large batches, while SGD variants are reported to fail at the two largest sizes. The stated epoch budget changes across sizes and conflicts with the appendix.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LAWN can improve recommendation ranking performance and batch scalability under the reported training budgets.

fits_no_version.finding: On MovieLens-1M, LAWN reports HR@10 of 70.41 and 70.77 versus weight decay's 70.12 and 69.28 at batches 10k and 100k, and exceeds the other listed loss-control methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LAWN can improve recommendation HR@10 relative to the tested methods for controlling loss of adaptivity.

fits_no_version.finding: In Figure 1, logit attenuation followed by constrained training reduces median training margin and eventually raises recommendation HR@10 above vanilla Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Logit attenuation followed by constrained training can improve recommendation ranking during continued Adam training.

record.code_released: not stated; paper says code link will be released after acceptance
record.problems: No train–test error gap is reported, and the paper evaluates LAWN rather than directly testing most of the catalog's claims. Experiments average 3 runs; standard errors are reported, but several recommendation results are summarized in text. ImageNet uses a modified LAMB+ comparator, and Adam beta and epsilon parameters were not tuned.
record.rows_left_out: The per-condition recommendation results in Tables 4 and 9–11 are summarized in R35 rather than expanded into individual model × optimizer × batch rows, to keep within 60 rows. These tables report separate HR@10 values and standard errors; Table 2 values are represented in R36. Other results and hyperparameter sweeps are omitted because they do not directly measure the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label held-out accuracy, and comparison with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their held-out error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and interventions on local connectivity or initialization.

Language benchmarks; training-performance comparisons; broad tuning of optimizer parameters; controlled tests of switching to SGD or decoupled versus coupled weight decay. CIFAR base optimizers additionally tune weight decay, so they do not isolate the learning-rate-and-schedule-only regime.

Language models; controlled longer-training interventions on the image workloads; and separate causal contributions of warmup, normalization and regularization. Recommendation results do not test the named workload scope.
Dropout interventions, small-training-set effects, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, measured generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- or margin-based measures. Discussion of sharp minima is not a test.
Identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: Direct adaptive-versus-SGD comparison rows for ImageNet. At batch 256: SGD 76.00 (0.04), Adam 71.16 (0.05), LAMB+ 74.30 (0.01), Adam-LAWN 76.18 (0.03), LAMB-LAWN 76.48 (0.05). At 16k: SGD 74.48 (0.06), Adam 70.60 (0.02), LAMB+ 73.43 (0.03), Adam-LAWN 76.07 (0.08), LAMB-LAWN 75.93 (0.02). Existing method-improvement rows do not encode these comparisons.

Direct adaptive-versus-SGD comparison rows for CIFAR at each batch. In order 256, 4k, 10k: CIFAR-10 SGD 93.99, 93.48, 92.99; Adam 93.48, 92.93, 92.63; Adam-LAWN 93.91, 93.74, 93.84; LAMB 93.76, 93.27, 92.91; LAMB-LAWN 93.67, 93.22, 92.92. CIFAR-100 SGD 73.49, 71.68, 71.07; Adam 70.84, 68.91, 68.61; Adam-LAWN 72.99, 73.12, 72.97; LAMB 71.29, 69.39, 67.76; LAMB-LAWN 71.25, 69.68, 69.16. Preserve Table 6's individual standard errors.

Intermediate CIFAR batch-size comparisons against 256 are missing for SGD, SGD-LAWN, LAMB and LAMB-LAWN. At 4k, CIFAR-10 accuracies are 93.48 (0.09), 93.50 (0.05), 93.27 (0.08), 93.22 (0.05), respectively; CIFAR-100 accuracies are 71.68 (0.26), 72.71 (0.07), 69.39 (0.06), 69.68 (0.16). Adam values at 4k also need explicit cross-batch comparisons rather than same-batch method comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. No train–test gap is required to test V4 or V5, which name held-out performance. Near-zero Adam-LAWN batch differences support V5's stated adapted-recipe exception rather than challenge the full conditional claim. Recommendation tables were explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so their unexpanded cells are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same recipe.
Width sweep past interpolation and corresponding test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity interventions.
Language benchmarks; broad tuning; switching from Adam to SGD; decoupled weight decay; word-level language models.
Language models; equal-epoch large-batch comparisons for every optimizer and dataset; longer training or recipe changes as controlled causal interventions.
Dropout comparisons, small training sets, and dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples.
